cases.heading: Inflated claims about importance and legacy
cases.positive: This landmark platform reshaped the entire industry.
cases.counterexample: The article explains the documented workflow without predicting its legacy.

cases.heading: Name-dropping to prove importance
cases.positive: Leading analysts and major institutions recognize the approach.
cases.counterexample: The article names a source only when that source supports the claim.

cases.heading: Shallow analysis with -ing phrases
cases.positive: The workflow improves visibility, helping teams move faster.
cases.counterexample: The workflow improves visibility because dispatch and finance share one record.

cases.heading: Sales language
cases.positive: This groundbreaking platform will revolutionize dispatch.
cases.counterexample: The scheduling view shows assigned jobs and open capacity.

cases.heading: Vague sources
cases.positive: Experts say job records improve performance.
cases.counterexample: A linked regulator report supplies the evidence for the statement.

cases.heading: Formulaic challenges and outlook sections
cases.positive: Despite these challenges, the future remains promising.
cases.counterexample: The final section answers the objective without a generic outlook.

cases.heading: Overused AI words
cases.positive: Delve into the ever-evolving scheduling landscape.
cases.counterexample: The AI scheduler uses the approved product name and supported description.

cases.heading: Avoiding is and are
cases.positive: The schedule serves as the operating record.
cases.counterexample: The schedule is the operating record.

cases.heading: Not X but Y and clipped negative endings
cases.positive: This is not just scheduling, but also profit control.
cases.counterexample: The FAQ compares two real options with evidence.

cases.heading: Forced groups of three
cases.positive: The workflow is faster, clearer, and smarter.
cases.counterexample: Use the number of points the evidence requires.

cases.heading: Changing names and repeating sentence openings
cases.positive: Lead source follows each job. Lead source stays visible. Lead source links spend to invoices.
cases.counterexample: Lead source follows each job. Dispatch retains it. Finance connects it to invoices.

cases.heading: False from X to Y ranges
cases.positive: The workflow covers everything from the first thought to lasting success.
cases.counterexample: The guide covers quoting through invoicing.

cases.heading: Passive voice and missing subjects
cases.positive: The invoice was created after the technician left.
cases.counterexample: The technician created the invoice after leaving.

cases.heading: Em and en dashes
cases.positive: Dispatch looks clean—until jobs move.
cases.counterexample: Use a period for prose and an en dash for the 2025–2026 range.

cases.heading: Too much bold text
cases.positive: **Every sentence is bold.**
cases.counterexample: Bold only the term readers need to scan.

cases.heading: Lists with bold mini-headings
cases.positive: - **Scheduling:** Assign the job.
cases.counterexample: Use a plain list when labels add no meaning.

cases.heading: Title case in headings
cases.positive: ## Scheduling For Field Teams
cases.counterexample: ## Scheduling for Field Teams

cases.heading: Emojis
cases.positive: 🚀 Launch the new workflow.
cases.counterexample: Use an emoji only when the channel treatment calls for it.

cases.heading: Curly quotation marks
cases.positive: He said “the job is complete.”
cases.counterexample: Keep the approved exact quotation unchanged.

cases.heading: Chatbot text left in the answer
cases.positive: I hope this helps. Feel free to ask for another version.
cases.counterexample: The article ends with the intended reader action.

cases.heading: Knowledge-limit disclaimers and guesses
cases.positive: As of my last update, the feature may exist.
cases.counterexample: The limitation identifies a verified scope boundary.

cases.heading: Overly agreeable tone
cases.positive: You are absolutely right about every point.
cases.counterexample: The blog evaluates the evidence without flattering the reader.

cases.heading: Filler phrases
cases.positive: Dispatchers just need one job record.
cases.counterexample:
### Is PPC just Google Ads?

No. PPC is a pricing model.

cases.heading: Too many qualifiers
cases.positive: The workflow could perhaps sometimes improve visibility.
cases.counterexample: The evidence may support a narrower claim.

cases.heading: Generic positive endings
cases.positive: The future is bright for every field team.
cases.counterexample: The conclusion states the supported next action.

cases.heading: Too many hyphenated word pairs
cases.positive: The end-to-end real-time workflow is user-friendly.
cases.counterexample: Real-time is retained as a necessary technical compound.

cases.heading: Pretending to reveal a deeper truth
cases.positive: The real issue is not scheduling. It is control.
cases.counterexample: The author labels judgment as opinion.

cases.heading: Announcing the next point
cases.positive: In conclusion, field teams need cleaner job data.
cases.counterexample: Field teams need cleaner job data.

cases.heading: A heading repeated in the first sentence
cases.positive:
## Scheduling

Scheduling keeps the calendar current.
cases.counterexample:
## Scheduling

The calendar shows assigned work and open capacity.

cases.heading: Writing about the previous version
cases.positive: The previous version used a different workflow.
cases.counterexample: The migration guide explains what changed from the earlier release.

cases.heading: Forced punchlines and dramatic fragments
cases.positive: One record. No excuses.
cases.counterexample: The author uses one short punchline where it improves emphasis.

cases.heading: Formulaic sayings
cases.positive: When the going gets tough, the tough get going.
cases.counterexample: The author uses a saying only when it is authentic and useful.

cases.heading: Fake-candid openings
cases.positive: Let us be honest, nobody likes paperwork.
cases.counterexample: In my experience, late job notes create avoidable rework.

cases.heading: Answering objections no one raised
cases.positive: You might think setup is difficult, but it is not.
cases.counterexample: The FAQ answers a documented buyer objection.

cases.heading: Rejecting fake alternatives
cases.positive: It is not email. It is not a spreadsheet. It is Simpro.
cases.counterexample: The comparison evaluates email, spreadsheets, and job management software.
